Both were measured without DH and DJ (DH's Java results did not exist when I measured; DJ is the re-check's batch) and are false over the full cohort set: review-6 counts 8 worse vs 1ad869dae and vs 9ed52f435, and 65 worse vs 28af44ab3 (38 approved, 20 packet-caused, 7 inherited).

obligation_1_numbering.java: data-source-line and codeLine are LineLocation positions (0-based) in the text BlockUmlBuilder reads. In -pipe mode that text is Pipe#readSingleDiagram's (Pipe.java:180-225). '@@@format ' lines are consumed by manageFormat and never appended (188-189). While NO_CONTENT, a line whose String#trim is empty is not appended (191-192, 207-208); the first other line moves to START_MARK_NOT_FOUND and every later line is appended. When no line startsWith("@start"), Pipe returns "@startuml\n" + sb (217), so the k-th appended line is at position k (the prepended line is 0).
obligation_1_numbering.rust_divergence: ea5375293 changed only PreprocessContext#current_diagram_source_line, which reaches only lines that carry a source-line marker (themes, includes, buffered and expression lines). Plain lines take their parser-stream position, which is the input line minus 1.
obligation_1_numbering.planned_change: merge_ending_backslash_lines computes, when Pipe finds no start mark, the Pipe-text position of every raw input line (the rule above). The context keeps it, numbers every line at include depth 0 by it (current_diagram_source_line), and marks every content line from the first line (mark_source_lines), so plain lines carry their Pipe position like marked ones. Inputs where Pipe finds its mark are unchanged; that includes every golden.
obligation_1_numbering.marked_inputs_not_changed: Pipe's discard of the lines before a column-0 mark (sb.setLength(0), 195) is NOT ported: the 8 goldens with lines before '@start' (multi-diagram/preproc_*) carry file-relative numbers (picoweb, not -pipe), so porting it would break them. r5b_num_comment_at_seq and o5s_ws_leading_blank_at stay residue; proposed target.

obligation_2_type.java: DiagramType#findStartTypes (DiagramType.java:69-92) then getTypes (94-216): a switch on Character.toLowerCase of the character right after 'start', then check(key) = regionMatches(ignoreCase) prefix tests in source order (b: bpm, board; c: chart, creole, chronology, chen; d: dot, ditaa, def; e: ebnf; f: flow, files; g: gantt, git; h: hcl; j: jcckit, json; l: latex; m: math, mindmap; n: nwdiag; p: project -> GANTT, packetdiag; r: regex; s: salt, sprites; u: uml -> SEQUENCE..; w: wire, wbs; y: yaml); anything else UNKNOWN, which PSystemBuilder#createPSystem (225-227) turns into PSystemUnsupported.
obligation_2_type.rust_divergence: detect_type takes the first whitespace word after 'start' (b24935a2d lower-cases it): '\start uml' types as uml, '\startumlish' as 'umlish', '\startproject' as 'project'.
obligation_2_type.planned_change: A port of getTypes maps the text after 'start' to the Rust dispatch key of its Java type (uml, json, yaml, mindmap, gantt (gantt and project), git, wbs, math, latex, salt, nwdiag, regex, ditaa, dot, board, ebnf). A Java type with no Rust parser (bpm, chart, creole, chronology, chen, def, flow, files, hcl, jcckit, packetdiag, sprites, wire) keeps its Java name, and UNKNOWN keeps the raw text after 'start'; neither is a dispatch key, so both are 'unsupported diagram type' errors, as '@startchen' is at every build.
obligation_2_type.declared_exception: r5b_start_bs_chen: Java renders CHEN_EER. Rust has no Chen parser ('@startchen' is unsupported at every build, the parent's out-of-scope note). 9ed52f435 rendered it only because '\startchen' was not a start line there, as an accidental CLASS diagram (data-diagram-type CLASS vs Java CHEN_EER). With Java's start test it is a CHEN block and Rust reports it unsupported: equal to the merged base c25ccbf3c, worse than 9ed52f435's accidental mismatch. No fallback that re-creates the accidental output is added; this is declared for the owner (Chen dispatch, or accept). r5b_start_bs_project types GANTT and dispatches to the gantt parser.

obligation_3_nbsp.java: BlockUmlBuilder#<init> (BlockUmlBuilder.java:91) reads through UncommentReadLine. UncommentReadLine#readLine (preproc/UncommentReadLine.java:61-81) calls StartUtils#beforeStartUml (StartUtils.java:56-80) on every line: for '\u00A0@startuml', U+00A0 is neither Character#isWhitespace nor isLetterOrDigit/'_'/'~', so the scan reaches '@start' at index 1 and returns the header '\u00A0'. headerToRemove becomes '\u00A0', and every later line starting with it loses it (a line that is a prefix of the header becomes ""). The line read by BlockUmlBuilder is therefore '@startuml', a start directive. Pipe's prepended '@startuml' sets headerToRemove to "", which strips nothing.
obligation_3_nbsp.rust_divergence: Rust ports UncommentReadLine only for wrapped includes (wrapped_diagram_lines). The main block is not uncommented, so '\u00A0@startuml' stays a content line (the tip's java_is_whitespace start test is right; the missing stage is UncommentReadLine).
obligation_3_nbsp.planned_change: The main-block input goes through the same UncommentReadLine port (before ReadFilterMergeLines, as in Java's reader chain), shared with wrapped_diagram_lines. split_blocks and detect_type test start and end lines on the uncommented text. Pause/unpause handling is not ported (paused stays false), as before.
